theme: conjecture shot: seal size and closing signs as marks of grade
question: Do the closing signs of Indus seal legends mark a grade that the seal's size also marks, beyond seal type, site and text length, and are opening signs more local than closing signs?
outcome: Discovery half (590 seals, one per component): the closing-sign size signal sat in four rare last signs (001, 595, 679, 820; 18 seals, +0.66 residual log area against -0.02); identical legends not closer in size (p 0.31). Frozen predictions scored once on the confirmation half (620 seals, 582 components): P4 pass, the 11 seals ending in the set +0.35 against -0.01 (p 0.021); P1a pass, last-sign between-sign ratio 1.81 (p 0.0074); P1b fail, frozen lexicon r 0.117 against rearrangements (p 0.060); P1c fail, closing not above opening (p 0.32); P2 fail, identical legends 0.445 against 0.512 (p 0.10); P3 fail and reversed, closing formulae site-specific (z 2.72) and first signs not (z -0.16); auxiliary P5 pass, unicorn Bull1:W seals +0.37 (p 0.0001). Kill condition not met; C-0001 credence 0.12 to 0.21. Independent recomputation agreed on P1a, P4 and the kill decision. Post-outcome (exploratory): the P4 pass rests mainly on 820 (5 seals, +0.62); 679 did not repeat; other closers carry size on the confirmation half (ratio 1.62, p 0.027).
challenge: The high set was chosen after looking from 28 signs and rests on 18 discovery and 11 confirmation seals; P1a, P1b and P4 share those seals; a layout reading (a large face leaves room for an extra final sign) predicts the same association; the coordinator's review followed Shot B's confirmation outcome; the site result reversed between halves.
remedy: Two-stage design with hashed predictions, lexicon and scoring code; split-half rehearsal and power simulation before freezing; stratified permutations keeping type, site and length; one seal per component; independent recomputation with separate code and generator; post-outcome analysis confined to a dated exploratory amendment.
retry_when: Seals outside this export (later excavation reports or a new concordance) with complete legends ending in 820, 001 or 595 and measured faces; photographs showing whether those closing signs sit inside the text band; or impressions on sealings whose legends end in these signs. Do not retest the full closing-sign lexicon or the opening-closing locality contrast on the same split.
